stories.headline: Dodgers acquire infielder Royce Lewis in trade with Twins
stories.summary: The Dodgers acquired infielder Royce Lewis in a trade with the Twins, fulfilling Los Angeles' need for a versatile right-handed hitter to replace Miguel Rojas.
stories.body:
The Los Angeles Dodgers acquired talented, oft-injured infielder Royce Lewis in a trade with the Minnesota Twins on Friday, fulfilling their need for a versatile right-handed hitter to replace the retiring Miguel Rojas.

Bobby Miller, a former prized starter who recently transitioned to the bullpen, is going to the Twins along with 19-year-old catching prospect Francisco Espinoza.

Lewis, 27, is projected by MLB Trade Rumors to make $5.1 million in arbitration in his second-to-last year before free agency and was a threat to be non-tendered ahead of Friday's deadline. In L.A., though, he fits precisely what the Dodgers were searching for this offseason: a right-handed hitter who can occasionally spell the left-handed-hitting Max Muncy and Freddie Freeman at first base while also drawing starts at second base.

Lewis spent ample time at all three of those positions with the Twins in 2026 while batting .227/.287/.380 with 15 home runs and 16 stolen bases in 125 games.

The 2017 No. 1 overall pick out of high school in San Juan Capistrano, California -- located 60 miles south of Dodger Stadium -- Lewis has mostly been defined by the injuries that robbed him of stardom. He debuted as a 22-year-old in 2022, but injuries to his right knee, oblique, hamstring and quad limited him to only 152 games over a three-year period -- during which he carried an .825 OPS with 33 home runs and 104 RBIs.

Lewis stayed mostly healthy in 2025 and 2026, totaling 231 games, but he produced 15% below the league average, according to OPS-plus.

By trading Lewis and not tendering offers to outfielder Trevor Larnach and right-handed starter Bailey Ober, the Twins lopped off approximately $18.3 million in payroll Friday.

Miller, 27, broke out as a starter in 2023, going 11-4 with a 3.76 ERA while showcasing a triple-digit fastball and a vicious curveball. He struggled mightily in the majors and minors over the next two years, however, and missed almost the entirety of the 2026 season with a shoulder injury.

stories.headline: Fantasy football Week 11 inactives: Who's in and who's out?
stories.summary: Updated inactives and analysis based on the latest reports and official announcements leading up to kickoff.
stories.body:
Biggest injury concerns for Week 11
Players with early starts
Carson Beck, QB, Cardinals (back): Beck popped up on Thursday's injury report with a back injury. He has dealt with this issue throughout the season and currently appears to be unlikely to play in Week 11. Josh Johnson would be next man and is purely a two-QB format option for those who are desperately in need of a bye week/injury replacement. In either event, Trey McBride is the only Cardinals player that should be started with any confidence -- and even his value is diminished in this new-look Cardinals offense.

Dalton Kincaid, TE, Bills (thumb/ankle): Kincaid has not yet practiced this week and is doubtful for Week 11. With the Bills playing the Chiefs on Thanksgiving -- just four days after this game -- expect Buffalo to use caution here. If he sits, Dawson Knox becomes a deeper streaming option against a Dolphins team that has allowed the fifth-most TE fantasy PPG.

Don't forget to check these out: Mike Clay's Playbook | Week 11 Buzz

Week 11 Rankings | Matchup rankings for Week 11

Official Sunday inactives should begin coming in approximately 90 minutes before the scheduled kickoff times: around 11:30 a.m. ET for the early games and 2:30 p.m. ET for the late-afternoon games.

Refresh often for the latest information.

Jonathon Brooks, RB, Panthers (groin): Brooks is questionable for Week 11, but seems close to making his return after having practiced in full all week. He is worth adding if he is available on your league's waiver wire, but fantasy managers should take a wait-and-see approach. Chuba Hubbard remains an RB1 play.

Darren Waller, TE, Panthers (knee): Waller is questionable for Week 11 after limited practices on Thursday and Friday. Waller is a TD-dependent streaming option. Some preferred TE plays are Mark Andrews and Chig Okonkwo. Waller should be used over Brenton Strange, Dallas Goedert and Mike Gesicki.

Kyle Monangai, RB, Bears (toe): Monangai is off the injury report, meaning he will play in week 11. He has not played since Week 4. Still, he is in the mix as a flex option due to a matchup against the Saints. New Orleans has allowed the fourth-most rushing yards to RBs, as well as the second-most RB fantasy points.

Caleb Douglas, WR, Dolphins (shoulder): Douglas had been limited at practice this week before elevating to full on Friday. He is off the injury report meaning he will play in Week 11. He has seen eight targets in both of his last two games and has scored double-digit fantasy points in three of his four games since returning from injury. While he is more volatile with QB Kyle McCord, Douglas is in the flex conversation, especially given all the byes.

Jordyn Tyson, WR, Saints (chest): Tyson has been limited at practice this week and is questionable for Week 11. If he plays, he'd be a WR3 (with a lot more upside). Tyson saw a 38% target share and 50% air yard share last week in his first NFL game with no limitations. In a game where the Saints will have to put up points, Tyson should be started.

DeVonta Smith, WR, Eagles (hamstring): Smith has practiced in full this week and is off the Eagles practice report, meaning he is set to make his return in Week 11. He will be the top target for Joe Milton and the Eagles. While his production likely takes a hit without Jalen Hurts in the huddle, Milton does throw a good deep ball. That could lead to some big plays for Smith. He should be valued as a low-end WR2 in his first game back on the field. Dontayvion Wicks (ankle/foot) will not return this week for the Eagles.

Michael Pittman Jr, WR, Steelers (foot): Pittman has not played since Week 3, but is practicing in full this week. He seems on track to return this week. While that's a boost for those streaming Aaron Rodgers this week, I would take a wait-and-see approach with Pittman. Not only is it his first game back, but the Steelers have struggled to get consistent production from their receivers. This does make Germie Bernard, who has been unproductive as of late, a firm sit. The only Steelers receiver worth starting is DK Metcalf. Roman Wilson (hand) is also questionable for the Steelers.

Baker Mayfield, QB, Buccaneers (ankle): Mayfield returned to practice on Thursday, which puts him on the right side of questionable. While Mayfield has not been a great fantasy option himself this season, his presence has elevated Tampa Bay's playmakers, especially Emeka Egbuka. Still, Mayfield is a streaming option this week against the Lions, who allow the second-most QB fantasy PPG.

Carnell Tate, WR, Titans (shoulder): Tate has been limited at practice this week and while he is questionable heis trending towards making a Week 11 return. From Weeks 3-7 (Tate's last five games), he had a 27% target share (11th-highest) and a 45% air yard share (third-highest). He was producing then, and certainly could do so again in this new-look Titans offense that has averaged 39.5 passing attempts per game over the last two weeks. Tate is a WR3 with upside.

Players with late starts
Jaylen Waddle, WR, Broncos (concussion): Waddle has practiced in full coming out of the Broncos bye week. He has been removed from the injury report and will play in Week 11. Waddle is a WR3 with upside in a favorable matchup against the Raiders. Las Vegas ranks in the top three in terms of the most yards and touchdowns allowed to wide receivers this season. With six teams on bye, it's worth taking a shot on Waddle this week.

Bhayshul Tuten, RB, Jaguars (ankle/foot): Tuten is off the injury report and will play in Week 11. He has been in and out of practice for the last couple of weeks but continues to play and be productive. Tuten has surpassed 20 fantasy points in three out of his last four games. If Tuten plays for the Jaguars, he should be started in fantasy football. It's worth noting that Chris Rodriguez Jr. (hand), who is the next man up, has also been limited at practice.

Brock Bowers, TE, Raiders (ankle): After exiting early in Week 10, Bowers returned to practice on Thursday. He is questionable for Week 11. When asked if he will play this week, Bowers said "we'll see", per ESPN reporter Ryan McFadden. If he suits up, he is an obvious must start. If he sits, Michael Mayer is a TE1 worth starting in a favorable matchup. Denver has allowed the third-most TE fantasy PPG. Mayer is still a potential flex option this week if Bowers suits up.

Ladd McConkey, WR, Chargers (back): He has been limited at practice this week after missing the last two games due to this back injury. He is questionable, but even if he suits up, the risk of him leaving early is high. McConkey has played well when he's been able to stay on the field this season. The issue is that he's played just two full games. Due to that fact, fantasy managers should play it safe and look to get away from McConkey for the time being.

Isaiah Likely, TE, Giants (undisclosed): Likely popped up on the injury report on Friday, with what John Harbaugh called a "minor injury." He was removed from the injury report on Friday and will be active on Sunday. Likley has reached must-start status whenever he suits up.

Geno Smith, QB, Jets (ankle): Smith has been limited at practice before upgrading to full on Friday. He is off the injury report meaning he will play in Week 11. Smith is a QB2 against a Chargers defense that has been tough against QBs. Some streaming options I'd prefer over Smith are Bo Nix, Cam Ward, Mayfield and J.J. McCarthy.

Players on Sunday night
T.J. Hockenson, TE, Vikings (wrist): Hockenson was limited at practice this week, before being upgraded to full participation on Friday. He is off the injury report and will play in Week 11. Consider him to be a low-end TE1. though I would rather play Mark Andrews or Chig Okonkwo. However, I would roll with Hockenson over Kincaid, Darren Waller or Brenton Strange.

Mike Evans, WR, 49ers (Achilles): Evans returned to practice in a limited fashion on Thursday. That gives him a chance to suit up this week, even though he is questionable. If he plays, he would be a WR2 who carries both upside and risk. The upside has been clear. The risk is re-injury or struggling in a tough matchup against the Vikings, who have allowed the fifth-fewest WR fantasy PPG. If he sits, Deebo Samuel Sr. would be Brock Purdy's top wideout -- and a fantasy WR3.

Players on Monday night
Jacory Croskey-Merritt, RB, Commanders (groin): JCM appears likely to make his return from IR on Monday against the Bengals. Rachaad White has led this backfield in his absence, but I would anticipate Croskey-Merritt will handle the bulk of ground work, with White as the passing-downs back -- a role that better suits him. Austin Ekeler is likely the odd man out.

Fantasy managers should ideally take a wait and see approach with Washington. However, with six teams on a bye, they may need to pivo to a Commanders RB. Either JCM or White would be deeper-league flex options. Croskey-Merritt brings a safer floor, but White has more upside since the Commanders could end up trailing and needing to throw a bunch in this one. However, it is worth noting that White was added to the injury report on Friday (heel), which has his availability in question. If he were to sit, Croskey-Merritt would become a more appealing option, with Ekeler being an option in deep leagues.

Ruled out before Sunday

Kenneth Walker III, RB, Chiefs (groin): The Chiefs are big favorites this weekend against the Cardinals and will face the Bills on Thanksgiving, just four days later. They have a number of big games to come. Due to that, they are practicing caution and have ruled Walker out for Week 11. Emmett Johnson becomes a must-start RB1 with Walker out this week.

Omar Cooper Jr., WR, Jets (ankle/hip): Cooper has not yet practiced this week and has been ruled out for for Week 11. Cooper has been banged up for a bit, so a week to recover will probably do him some good. He is worth stashing if you have the space on your bench. In his absence, expect Adonai Mitchell to see more targets. Mitchell should be a considered a "boom-or-bust" flex option against the Chargers who have allowed the sixth-most WR fantasy PPG.

Wan'Dale Robinson, WR, Titans (ankle): Robinson has been placed on IR and is out for the remainder of the season. That should mean more volume for Tate, when healthy. It also makes Elic Ayomanor an upside stash worth grabbing off the waiver wire, if he is still available in your league.

stories.headline: Hirving Lozano returns to San Diego FC as LA Galaxy loan ends
stories.summary: The LA Galaxy declined to exercise their purchase option for Hirving 'Chucky' Lozano, sending the Mexican forward back to San Diego FC.
stories.body:
LA Galaxy announced the club will not exercise the option to permanently acquire Hirving "Chucky" Lozano after his loan spell, as the forward returns to San Diego FC ahead of the 2027 sprint season.

"Hirving Lozano has completed his loan with the Galaxy and returned to his parent club, San Diego FC," the Galaxy announced in a press release when it made its 2026 roster decisions public.

The Galaxy signed Lozano on loan as a Designated Player in August through December 2026, with a permanent trade option included in the contract. He played 10 matches for the club, recording two goals and one assist, before the Galaxy made the decision to end his time with the club.

Lozano originally signed with San Diego FC in June 2025 while still under contract with PSV Eindhoven, months ahead of the expansion team's MLS debut. He finally joined the club in January, playing 27 matches in their inaugural season before conflict led him to the sidelines.

The Mexican forward was first left off the roster for San Diego FC's first-ever MLS playoff match following a report of a locker room altercation. Head coach Mikey Varas hinted that Lozano could be back with the team soon.

Lozano publicly apologized for his reaction inside the locker room before tensions escalated.

By January 2026, sporting director Tyler Heaps and Varas confirmed Lozano would no longer be taken into consideration.

"Our stance remains the same," sporting director Tyler Heaps told ESPN ahead of the team's 2026 season opener. "Hirving is not and will not be part of our sporting plans heading into this year."

Lozano trained independently for months before eventually signing with the Galaxy in August. It remains unclear what his role with San Diego will be in 2027 following his return from the loan spell.

The Galaxy also announced that veteran defender Maya Yoshida will depart after captaining the club for three and a half seasons. The Japan international made 117 appearances across all competitions and was a cornerstone of the squad that captured the club's sixth MLS Cup title in 2024.

stories.summary: The NBA is back. The buzz never left. Bookmark this page for the latest news, rumblings and analysis from ESPN's insiders.
stories.body:
The NBA's leaguewide buzz never stops.

The LeBron James and Jaylen Brown era with the Philadelphia 76ers has gotten off to an ideal start while the Detroit Pistons and Boston Celtics have also proved that the Eastern Conference is going to be a gauntlet this season. In the West, the Oklahoma City Thunder are managing a collection of injuries while the rival San Antonio Spurs sit atop the conference with the Los Angeles Lakers.

The season is less than a month in but the league's landscape is starting to take shape as new faces in new places are making their impact. Which team will make the first move that influences the championship picture?

All season, bookmark this page for the latest news and reactions from ESPN's NBA insiders.

Shams: Injury updates on Haliburton, Leonard and Harper
ESPN's Shams Charania went on NBA Today and gave injury updates on Tyrese Haliburton, Kawhi Leonard and Dylan Harper.

Haliburton (hamstring) will miss "at least" a couple more weeks for the Indiana Pacers. The Toronto Raptors are optimistic about Leonard (knee) returning to action in the "next few weeks". Plus, San Antonio Spurs young guard Harper (hip) is expected to miss 1-3 weeks.

'Hoop Collective': Are the Lakers relying too much on Luka?
Brian is joined by ESPN's Tim MacMahon and Ben Golliver to talk about whether Luka Doncic's historic usage rate is a concern for the Lakers moving forward and whether L.A. has the ability to lessen his workload.

Next, they break down new comments from Anthony Edwards about his injury and the timeline for his potential return. Finally, the trio discusses how the Suns are starting to turn things around, Jamal Murray's impressive play for Denver and some key players who deserve more recognition.

Golliver on Doncic's historic start: "The question always becomes about sustainability, diminishing returns, can you keep this up? Is it the healthiest way to play? ... I mostly wanted to write this piece not as an angel of death, saying, 'Oh, it's not going to work,' but to look at comparisons between Luka and some of those other guys to see, 'Could this be the forefront of basketball?' Have they figured out a way to calibrate this so Luka can go out there and do everything, and it actually pays off pretty well for the team?

"I do think we need to dig in a little bit to Luka versus Harden or Luka versus Russ to see, 'does this make sense as a championship formula?' Because hanging over this is that there's never been a player with a usage above 35 to win a championship, right? Not Jordan ... not Kobe. Usually, they're down in the low 30s, and Luka is above 40 right now. And so usually that's a red flag when people are looking at this."

MacMahon and Windhorst on rumors of Suns-Pelicans trade talks:

MacMahon: "Well, [Jalen Green]'s been in the trade rumor mill. There's been a lot of Dejounte Murray for Jalen Green smoke. What I can tell you is that smoke is not coming from Phoenix. It is certainly not something that these Suns are excited about. And if that sort of a trade is going to materialize, the value is not going to be Dejounte Murray. The value is going to be whatever pick that the Pelicans would be willing to put in that deal.

"And if you're the Pelicans, you absolutely shouldn't even be considering putting a kind of pick in a deal like that."

Windhorst: "Well, let's be honest. The two teams have talked about it, and the Suns didn't hang up the phone. There have been discussions."

Spurs' Harper (hip) out 1-3 weeks

San Antonio Spurs guard Dylan Harper has been diagnosed with a left hip rotator strain, avoiding any major injury, sources tell ESPN's Shams Charania. There is a one- to three-week timetable for Harper's return, dependent on his rehab.

Hoop Collective: Memphis is one of the most interesting teams in the NBA
Brian is joined by ESPN's Tim MacMahon to break down why the Memphis Grizzlies are one of the most interesting teams in the league, including the unique approach the franchise is taking in team building. They also compare the Grizzlies' turnaround to the Washington Wizards' rough start and discuss whether Anthony Davis could be traded again. Next, they discuss if the teams attempting "the flip" -- Utah Jazz, Brooklyn Nets, Wizards -- are having any success. They close on how the Minnesota Timberwolves are surviving without Anthony Edwards and the Boston Celtics looking like a legitimate contender.

MacMahon on Washington's options with Davis: "The AD thing, look, it's going to reach a point before the trade deadline where you've got to make a decision, and that's either trade him or pay him. And I think there are big problems with either of those scenarios because if you're paying him, unless there's a significant turnaround, you've got a really expensive team that needs to improve to reach mediocrity. That's not a good thing.

"Trading him, everybody who's trading for him is looking at that saying, 'OK, what kind of contract do we have to give him?' How much does that impact what we're willing to offer?" And again, this is the exact thing the [Dallas] Mavericks ran into and the Mavericks were able to unload some some other salaries in that deal and say, 'We didn't get much in return, but we at least got off a bunch of money.'

"It's just going to be hard to make a trade of Anthony Davis that's going to win any press conferences or impress your bosses."

Spears: Warriors could move on from vets ahead of deadline

Andscape's Marc J. Spears said on NBA Today that the Golden State Warriors could be in position to make a major deal at the trade deadline, but for such a move to be consummated, they may have to include one of the big contracts from such veterans as Jimmy Butler, Draymond Green and/or Kristaps Porzingis.

"I think they need to be aggressive at the trade deadline," Spears said. "They have some pieces to do it, people that have been there for a while. Draymond [Green], Jimmy [Butler]. I do expect the Warriors to make some kind of splash at the deadline."

NBA Trade Lab: Dejounte Murray's trade request

After formally requesting a trade last Friday, New Orleans Pelicans guard Dejounte Murray has unsurprisingly been the player most involved in fan-created trades over the past seven days in our NBA Trade Lab.

The Spurs traded Murray to the Hawks in 2022 for a massive haul: three first-round picks (including the Hawks' pick in the upcoming 2027 draft) and one first-round pick swap. At the time, Murray was viewed as a burgeoning young star with a strong impact on both sides of the ball. In Atlanta he expanded his offensive game, but his defensive impact, as measured by Net Points, fell off a cliff. In 2024, the Hawks sent him to the Pelicans in exchange for a package that included two first-round picks and Dyson Daniels, who went on to win Most Improved Player the following season.

Now in 2026, it appears likely Murray will be on the move again, but his market is difficult to read. His impact metrics have been on the decline, and he's making over $30 million for the next two seasons after turning 30 years old. At the same time, he is undoubtedly a talented player who could certainly find a renaissance in the right situation. Let's look at some of the top fan-created trades to see what fans are thinking might be a realistic deal.

Trade No. 1
Pelicans get: Jalen Green

Phoenix Suns get: Dejounte Murray

Green and Murray are similar in many ways, so a straight-up swap could make sense for both teams. Green is a talented scorer, but he lacks consistency and doesn't offer the ancillary skills to buoy him at a constant floor of positive impact. He is also only 24, the same age as Warriors Rookie of the Year candidate Yaxel Lendeborg, so the Pelicans could see room to further develop him in their system.

For the Suns, this would be a bet on their system. They have built a menacing defensive identity over the past two seasons and often punch above their weight through effort and hustle. Bringing Murray into this system could help to revive some of the defensive aspects of his game that have faded in recent years.

Trade No. 2
Pelicans get: Four second-round picks

Charlotte Hornets get: Murray

In this unusual deal, the Pelicans get no players back. It is a valid trade because of the $40 million trade exception that the Hornets received in the LaMelo Ball trade. Four second-round picks may not sound like much, but in the process the Pelicans would also open up a $32 million trade exception of their own and would completely clear Murray's money off their books without receiving any undesirable contracts in return.

The Hornets' offense has been really struggling this season, ranking last in Offensive Net Points per game, after losing their offensive engine in LaMelo Ball. Trading for Murray could inject some life into their offense, strengthening their guard play while they wait for Kon Knueppel to return from injury and Coby White to return to form after a slow start to his season.

Trade No. 3
Pelicans get: De'Aaron Fox and Spurs 2029 first-round pick

San Antonio Spurs get: Murray and Herb Jones

The Pelicans here get a proven winner and veteran presence in Fox, who could help to mentor Jeremiah Fears and their other young players throughout their roster. They also receive a 2029 first-round pick to build their future draft capital.

The Spurs are rolling right now and Fox has been playing great, so this would likely be a trade they consider only if things start to go downhill a bit and they decide they want to get off Fox's contract. San Antonio might be more interested in Murray than other teams, since he played some of his best basketball there. In this deal they also receive a very valuable player in Jones, whose defensive ability could slot perfectly into the Spurs' lineups and make the Victor Wembanyama-anchored defense even more impenetrable. -- Benjamin Tiemeyer

Have any more ideas on what move the Pelicans should make involving Dejounte Murray? Build it in the NBA Trade Lab, then submit your trade to let fans vote on it from both sides.

Jackson out with injured left foot
The Memphis Grizzlies announced GG Jackson sustained a break in the fifth metatarsal of his left foot on Saturday. He will have surgery and the timeline for his return will be announced after the procedure.

Hoop Collective: Trouble building in New Orleans? Time to trade Zion?

Brian is joined by ESPN's Tim MacMahon to cover Dejounte Murray's recent trade request in New Orleans, including what it means with Zion Williamson's future with the franchise. They then move on to the Miami Heat's recent hot streak and the Denver Nuggets' recent upswing despite an offensive dip from Nikola Jokic.

MacMahon on a potential Zion Williamson trade: "The trade market really doesn't even open for another month, when all the guys who signed their contracts last summer, or at least most, would be eligible. So this is all like very preliminary type of talk, but it's like people are talking about Zion just because he is a talent.

"He's the kind of player who people, as they're discussing possibilities of things happening around the league, like if that kind of talent is going to be available, it's something that people in front offices and people like us are going to at least kind of wonder about. And I've talked to several people about it, and the consensus that I've gotten is, 'Hey, there will be interest in Zion, but there's not going to be a blockbuster type of return.'

"And, one thing that's come up on multiple occasions is the return that the [Charlotte] Hornets ended up getting for LaMelo Ball, which was a talent upside swing. Charlotte clearly came to the decision that they wanted it to to move on. And that was a pretty good player, Naz Reid, and filler. And I think there was a couple seconds.

"And so I think that you're looking at maybe a first-round pick and then, I can sit here and speculate concepts that I think would be interesting. You don't put Zion on the block if you're Joe Dumars and expect that your phone's going to blow up with the kind of package that, for example, Milwaukee got for Giannis [Antetokounmpo]."

Nov. 13

Murray, Pelicans working toward trade
New Orleans Pelicans guard Dejounte Murray wants a trade from the franchise, and his agent, Klutch Sports CEO Rich Paul, and team officials have started working on a resolution, sources tell ESPN's Shams Charania.

Murray has made it clear he is ready to play a key role in meaningful basketball elsewhere. The Pelicans are 4-8 to start the season and have lost four games in a row, including a 145-111 blowout at home to the Brooklyn Nets on Wednesday.

From Bobby Marks: Murray signed a four-year $114 million extension with Atlanta in July 2023 but was traded the following offseason to New Orleans. He has two years remaining on his contract -- $32.8 and $30.8 million, respectively, with a player option in the second year.

One salary-cap nugget a team interested in Murray will have to consider is the $2.4 million in unlikely bonuses. While he did not reach any of the incentives in the previous season, unlikely bonuses are applied to the first and second apron. With Murray on their books, New Orleans is $4 million below the luxury tax and $5.7 million under the first apron hard cap.

Despite five players (including the $44.9 million nonguaranteed contract of Zion Williamson) earning more than $21 million in 2027-28, New Orleans is well positioned below the luxury tax and apron.

After not having a first-round pick in the 2026 draft, New Orleans could have two picks in the top four in 2027 -- its own and Milwaukee's. If one of those picks falls between Nos. 5 and 30, the least favorable would go to Atlanta.

MacMahon on the Lakers managing their injuries: "Sounds like it's a heel contusion [for Reaves].

"So, that's not a serious injury. You know, we'll see how long he needs to sit to get that right. I'm willing to bet that Luka is telling him, 'Hey, take your time with it. Make sure that you're right. Make sure that you're not favoring.'

Marks: A busy weekend of transaction expected
The last weekend of the offseason is expected to bring a flurry of transactions.

Starting on Saturday Oct. 17, teams will need to decide on players signed to non-guaranteed contracts. If a player is on the roster past 5 p.m. ET, teams will begin incurring a per day salary charge.

For example, the New York Knicks would be charged $17,622 per day against the cap if James Wiseman is not waived by Saturday. However, despite a mandate to remain under the second apron, New York is allowed to keep Wiseman and Bruce Brown to start the season.

The deadline for rookie extensions is Monday by 6 p.m. ET.

Since the start of the offseason, five players -- Victor Wembanyama, Amen and Ausar Thompson, Keyonte George and Brandin Podziemski -- have signed rookie extensions. The 2023 rookie class of extended players are below the per year average of 11 players we have seen since 2023.

Some of the notable names to watch include Brandon Miller and Cason Wallace. Keep in mind that out of the 34 players who signed rookie extensions in the prior three seasons, 17 came on the last day of eligibility.

The rookie extension deadline is not the only date teams are paying attention to, however. Oct. 19 is also the deadline to extend veterans who have two years left on their contract -- not including an option year -- and the last day to reduce rosters to 15 players on standard contracts. -- Bobby Marks

LeBron addressed his role too, saying he's open to whatever the team needs from him to win.

"Whatever they need me to do," he said. "The luxury of my game is I can do everything. ... Literally, I can do everything"

Kawhi: I was a distraction, ready to move forward
In his first public appearance with the Toronto Raptors after a controversy-filled summer, Kawhi Leonard addressed the NBA's investigation into him and his business dealings.

"I know why some of you guys came. You want to hear about the investigation. But in talking with the NBA and PA, I think the best decision is to move forward and focus on my time being a Toronto Raptor," he said. "I already was a distraction for the past 70 days and wasn't able to meet my teammates or do any of that stuff, minicamp stuff, so, moving forward, I just want to talk about the Toronto Raptors."

Haliburton: I am 100% healthy
Indiana Pacers guard Tyrese Haliburton said Monday that he is healthy and ready for the season.

"I am healthy. I am 100%," he said. "There will be no restrictions. That is not news. There is no source. I am the source. I am ready to go for the year."

Porzingis out indefinitely in blow to Warriors
Golden State Warriors big man Kristaps Porzingis is out indefinitely to open training camp with a health issue, according to the team.
In late July, Porzingis agreed to a two-year, $40 million contract with a player option on the second season to return to the Warriors.

Brown: KAT, Hart extension talks won't be a distraction
After reports surfaced last week that negotiations between the New York Knicks and center Karl-Anthony Towns had hit a stalemate, coach Mike Brown said Monday neither Towns' situation nor Hart's would linger in the locker room.

"We talk about everything [with the team]," Brown said. "We don't want to have any elephants in the room."

"I'm not involved in it. They'll figure it out. Control what you can control."

And here's what Towns said about a potential extension: "I've made it known I want to play here. Been a fan since I was a kid. I'd like to get it done."

Hornets GM: Brandon Miller to be ready for training camp
After undergoing offseason surgery on his left shoulder, Hornets wing Brandon Miller should be a full participant in training camp and "ready to roll" for opening night, Hornets general manager Jeff Peterson said Monday.

Miller, 23, is entering his fourth NBA season after being the No. 2 pick in the 2023 draft.

Duren won't be at Pistons media day, start of camp
Detroit Pistons All-Star center Jalen Duren is not attending the team's media day on Monday or the start of training camp as his contract standoff continues, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Monday.

Duren, a restricted free agent, is declining the team's five-year, $200 million fully guaranteed offer as both sides remain at a stalemate ahead of the Thursday deadline on a one-year, $9.6 million qualifying offer, sources said.

Bulls trade Dillingham to Hornets for Hield, cash
The Chicago Bulls and Charlotte Hornets agreed to a trade sending Rob Dillingham to Charlotte for Buddy Hield and cash, the teams announced Saturday.

2026 NBA offseason trade grades

What's next for Curry and the Warriors?
Stephen Curry's two-year, $116 million extension made him the first player in NBA history to amass $600 million in career on-court earnings.

The deal has also put the Golden State Warriors in position to have extra spending power next summer.

By Curry taking $10 million less than the maximum allowed, the Warriors project to have nearly $38 million in cap space in 2027. Golden State could increase its projection to $55 million if center Kristaps Porzingis is waived in the offseason. Porzingis' $20 million salary for next season is guaranteed for $3 million.

For Golden State to have ample room, forwards Draymond Green and Jimmy Butler III would need to sign elsewhere or at a significantly lesser salary. They will be free agents next summer.

Both salary projections include the $17 million free agent hold of guard Brandin Podziemski. The 2023 first-round pick is eligible until Oct. 19 to extend his contract. -- Bobby Marks

Hornets star Knueppel sidelined by hamstring injury
The Charlotte Hornets announced that Kon Knueppel will be out for at least the entire preseason because of a left hamstring injury.

James: Maxey, Embiid were factors in joining 76ers
LeBron James said his longstanding friendship with All-Star Tyrese Maxey and a desire to help Joel Embiid win his first NBA title played significant roles in his decision to sign a two-year, $8 million contract with the Philadelphia 76ers in July.

"[Embiid has] done everything in our league, and the only thing he has not done is win a championship. And I want to try to help him get that first one," James said. "He has a city on his back. He's been 'The Process' for 10 years, 12 years, however long he's been there. But I think it's time we even get you deeper into the process. And I hope that I can be, kind of, that final little piece that can help him get over the hump."

Grizzlies waive Russell
The Memphis Grizzlies have waived D'Angelo Russell, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Russell has made one All-Star team during his career and was selected No. 2 in the 2015 NBA draft.

stories.headline: Tom Brady tops list of athletes who became owners
stories.summary: The legendary quarterback is a member of an exclusive list of athletes that includes LeBron James, Serena Williams and Wayne Gretzky.
stories.body:
Tom Brady is getting (back) into the ownership game.

On Friday, sources confirmed to ESPN and NFL Network that the former superstar quarterback had bought shares in the English soccer giants Chelsea. Brady's purchasing of Chelsea shares comes after he departed the ownership group of another English club, EFL Championship side Birmingham City, earlier in the month after originally becoming a minority owner with a 3.3% stake.

Brady's latest interest isn't his only foray into the world of ownership -- he also owns a 5% minority stake in the Las Vegas Raiders, purchased in 2024, and he also has a stake in the Las Vegas Aces.

The NFL legend is far from the first athlete, active or former, to enter the ownership sphere. Here are other athletes who are now team owners:

Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Atlético Madrid

In October 26 news broke that the star Oklahoma City Thunder guard would be joining the club as an investor.

"I am excited to officially join the group of shareholders of Atlético de Madrid," Gilgeous-Alexander said in the club's post. "This is a club with a long history at the top of European football, and I am grateful for the opportunity to be part of its future."

Jason Kidd -- Everton

In April 2025, English Premier League club Everton announced that then-Dallas Mavericks coach Jason Kidd would be adding a different title to his résumé: ownership group member. The news came after Kidd joined Roundhouse Capital Holdings, which is part of the Friedkin Group -- the U.S. firm that completed its takeover of Everton's ownership the previous December.

Vince Carter, Tracy McGrady, Jozy Altidore -- Buffalo Bills

In December 2024, the Bills announced Carter, McGrady and Altidore were among 10 limited partners the team was adding to its ownership group. Both McGrady (New York Knicks) and Altidore (New York Red Bulls) played for New York-area teams, while Carter spent time with the Brooklyn Nets (who were known as the New Jersey Nets at the time) and was McGrady's teammate on the Toronto Raptors (who are closer to Buffalo than NYC-based teams).

Tom Brady -- Las Vegas Aces, Las Vegas Raiders, Chelsea

The Las Vegas Aces, the reigning WNBA champions, have added to their championship credentials. Seven-time Super Bowl champion Tom Brady acquired a minority stake in the team whose majority owner is Las Vegas Raiders owner Mark Davis.

"I have always been a huge fan of women's sports, and I admire the work that the Aces' players, staff, and the WNBA continue to do to grow the sport and empower future generations of athletes," Brady said in a statement. "To be able to contribute in any way to that mission as a member of the Aces organization is an incredible honor."

Brady attended an Aces game in May 2022 and sent gifts to star Kelsey Plum. Plum and other Aces players were excited to have Brady as part of the team.

He also added the Las Vegas Raiders to his resume after his purchase of minority stake in the franchise was approved by NFL teams owners on Tuesday. The deal was agreed on in May 2023, but it took owners 17 months to give their approval over concerns he was receiving too much of a discount from majority owner Mark Davis.

Brady was also a minority owner of Birmingham City, a club in English soccer's second-tier Championship, but sold his shares in November 2026. He purchased shares in Chelsea later that month.

Lewis Hamilton -- Denver Broncos

The Broncos' ownership group added racing royalty in August 2022. Formula One driver Lewis Hamilton has a stake with the Walton-Penner group, which purchased the team in June 2022.

Hamilton, 37, has the Formula One record for most race wins and has won the Formula One title seven times. The ownership group, which purchased the team for $4.65 billion, is led by Walmart heir Rob Walton and includes former U.S. Secretary of State Condoleezza Rice, who also has a stake.

In April, Hamilton joined with Serena Williams in a consortium led by former Liverpool chairman Martin Broughton in an attempt to buy Premier League club Chelsea.

"He is a champion competitor who knows what it takes to lead a winning team," Walton said in a statement.

Marshawn Lynch -- Seattle Kraken

Lynch spent 13 seasons in Seattle with the Seahawks, but his new sports venture in the state of Washington is on the ice. On April 18, he joined the Seattle Kraken ownership team as a minority investor. The former NFL running back will be a part of the NHL's "Hockey is for Everyone" campaign and Kraken owner Tod Leiweke said Lynch expressed interest in shadowing him to learn hockey CEO operations.

"This is something I never would have imagined," Lynch said to CNBC in a statement. "I always dreamed of playing on a professional team but owning one is something special. As I look back on some of my accomplishments...I'm [going to] continue to count my blessings."

Grammy Award-winning artist and Seattle native Macklemore also joined the Kraken ownership team with Lynch.

Wayne Gretzky, Steve Nash and Dustin Johnson -- Las Vegas Desert Dogs

Wayne Gretzky is a big lacrosse guy? Yep, you read that right. The Great One may have made his name on the ice, but before Gretzky was the pride of the Edmonton Oilers he was a bona fide lax bro.

"The national sport of Canada is box lacrosse," Gretzky said. "I started playing lacrosse on a team at the age of six and played all the way until I was 16 years old. I have a great love for the game in the sense I really think that box lacrosse was such a crucial part of the success I ultimately had in ice hockey."

Because of this, it shouldn't be completely surprising that the hockey legend is linking up with 2020 Masters champion Dustin Johnson, NBA Hall of Famer and current Brooklyn Nets head coach Steve Nash and Nets owner Joe Tsai as part of a star-studded ownership group for the National Lacrosse League's newest expansion team in Las Vegas, the Desert Dogs.

Dwyane Wade -- Utah Jazz

Seeing Dwyane Wade support any team other than the Miami Heat is decidedly jarring. In April, the three-time NBA champion purchased an ownership stake in the Utah Jazz, joining majority owner and team governor Ryan Smith, and expressed a desire to take an active role in the franchise. D. Wade made good on his promise. He could be seen courtside throughout the season; he took action when an unsettling fan incident went down during the postseason, and he became a mentor to then-Jazz star Donovan Mitchell.

The former Miami Heat star also added to his portfolio with something a bit closer to home. Wade, a Chicago native, joined the ownership group of the WNBA's Chicago Sky.

"It's a great opportunity to be a part of the league in its very early stages. ... Growth is going to happen, and so I want to be a part of the growth of this league," Wade said.

Kevin Durant -- Philadelphia Union, NJ/NY Gotham FC

In June 2020, Brooklyn Nets star Kevin Durant purchased a 5% stake in MLS' Philadelphia Union, and he has an option to purchase an additional 5% at a later date. Durant also had engaged in talks about purchasing part of D.C. United the year prior, but he said the discussion never progressed.

Durant expanded his portfolio in May of this year, after being named as a minority owner of the National Women's Soccer League (NWSL) club NJ/NY Gotham FC.

Thirty Five Ventures (35V), a company co-founded by the two-time NBA champion and entrepreneur Rich Kleiman, made a significant investment to acquire a stake in the club, marking the company's second investment in a professional soccer team.

Renee Montgomery -- Atlanta Dream

Former Atlanta Dream guard Renee Montgomery made history in February as part of a three-member investor group that was approved to purchase the team. Montgomery is the first former player to become both an owner and executive of a WNBA franchise. The ownership change followed pressure on former Republican Sen. Kelly Loeffler to sell her share of the Dream, after she angered WNBA players with her opposition to the league's racial justice initiatives.

Patrick Mahomes -- Kansas City Royals

Patrick Mahomes is no stranger to winning. While the Kansas City Royals can't exactly say the same, you can't rule out that the quarterback's winning ways might rub off on the franchise now that he is part of their ownership group. If Mahomes' status as an icon in Kansas City was in question (it wasn't), this move surely cemented it. Becoming a baseball owner made sense on several levels for the Chiefs' QB1. Not only was Mahomes -- who played baseball in college -- a legitimate pro prospect, his father, Pat Mahomes, spent 11 seasons in Major League Baseball. He also had to find some way to put that $503 million contract extension to good use.

Venus and Serena Williams -- Miami Dolphins, Angel City FC

Winning major titles and making history, that's what the Williams sisters do. In 2009, Venus and Serena became the first Black female minority owners in the NFL by purchasing a part of the Miami Dolphins. Musicians Jimmy Buffett, Gloria and Emilio Estefan, Fergie and Marc Anthony also bought shares in the team -- the Dolphins' ownership group is nothing if not eclectic. Then, last year, Serena Williams became part of the star-studded Angel City FC ownership group bringing a NWSL team to Los Angeles in 2022.

Mia Hamm, Abby Wambach and Julie Foudy -- Angel City FC

When Angel City FC arrived on the scene it did so in style. Before we even knew the Los Angeles based NWSL club's name, we knew it had superstar backing like no other. Among the 14 former USWNT players who are part of the group are Mia Hamm, Abby Wambach and Julie Foudy. I would have named Lauren Holiday, Shannon Boxx, Rachel Buehler, Amanda Cromwell, Joy Fawcett, Tisha Venturini Hoch, Angela Hucles, Shannon MacMillan, Saskia Webber and sisters Lorrie Fair Allen and Ronnie Fair Sullins, but I was really trying to stay true to my whole "I'm only going to name 20 athletes" thing from the intro. There are also a bunch of celebrities in the mix, but we don't have that kind of time.

Michael Jordan -- Charlotte Hornets

While we're on the subject of owners who haven't had the type of success we grew accustomed to in their playing days, I would be remiss if I didn't mention the GOAT. In 2010, Michael Jordan became the first ex-player to be a majority owner in the league when the NBA's Board of Governors unanimously approved his $275 million bid to buy the then Charlotte Bobcats in his home state of North Carolina. After a decade of underwhelming years, things look to be on the up for the now Hornets with Rookie of the Year LaMelo Ball providing a long-awaited spark in the organization. Never forget when his dad said he could beat MJ one-on-one ... good times.

Alex Rodriguez -- Minnesota Timberwolves, Minnesota Lynx

I don't know what part of this purchase feels less ideal to me, that Alex Rodriguez and his 50-50 business partner Marc Lore are only pursuing acquiring the Minnesota Timberwolves and Lynx after their original plan to buy the New York Mets failed or that Timberwolves star Anthony Edwards had no idea who former MLB star A-Rod was. Either way, the $1.5 billion deal is expected to close around July 1.

David Beckham -- Inter Miami

David Beckham, iconic soccer player and remains-to-be-seen owner. Beckham -- who is incredibly hands on with the franchise -- is part of an ownership group which was initially called Miami Beckham United but now operates under the name Miami Freedom Park LLC. Beckham and Inter Miami have seemingly been riddled with controversy since the club's inception in 2018. But all those problems could be a thing of the past if Lionel Messi decides to head to MLS. Hey, stranger things have happened.

LeBron James -- Liverpool

Back in 2011, LeBron James and manager Maverick Carter became minority owners of Premier League club Liverpool after Fenway Sports Group, which purchased the team in 2010, became the sole marketer of James' global rights. The deal has turned out to be pretty lucrative for James -- his original stake in the club, valued at about $6.5 million, had grown to about $32 million as of 2018. In 2019, Liverpool won the Premier League for their first top-flight league title in thirty years.

James Harden -- Houston Dynamo, Houston Dash

James Harden might not be in Houston anymore, but the former Rockets superstar's presence is still felt in the city. The Beard purchased a 5% stake in the group that controls MLS' Houston Dynamo and NWSL's Houston Dash in 2019. Boxer Oscar De La Hoya is also part of the group. The Dash won their first NWSL title last year, so he's probably feeling pretty good about that investment.

Russell Wilson and Ken Griffey Jr. -- Seattle Sounders

What do Russell Wilson, Ken Griffey Jr. and Macklemore have in common? They are all part of the Seattle Sounders' ownership group. Wilson, along with his wife, musician Ciara, purchased a stake in the team in 2019 -- just in time for them to win an MLS Cup title. Griffey Jr. and his family followed suit in November 2020.

Zlatan Ibrahimovic -- Hammaraby

Seemingly everything Zlatan does makes people react intensely, and that remained true when he purchased part of Swedish team Hammaraby back in 2019. Fans of Malmo, another Swedish team where Zlatan started his professional career, reacted by vandalizing a statue of Zlatan outside the team's home stadium, placing a toilet seat around one of its arms.

Magic Johnson -- Los Angeles Dodgers

Big LA guy. In 2012, Lakers great Magic Johnson was part of a group that bought the Los Angeles Dodgers from Frank McCourt for a record $2 billion. At the time, the price shattered the mark for a sports franchise. Magic kept it real at the time of purchase when explaining his role in recruiting free agents, saying that while he can't talk hitting or pitching with players, he "can talk winning." If recent history is any indication (in case you blacked out all of 2020 -- the Dodgers won the World Series), it worked.

stories.headline: Champions League upstarts Como suffer Moise Kean injury blow
stories.summary: Como forward Moise Kean is set to be out injured for at least two months and could miss Champions League games against Paris Saint-Germain and Barcelona.
stories.body:
Como forward Moise Kean is set to be out injured for at least two months, his coach Cesc Fabregas said on Friday, and could miss Champions League games against Paris Saint-Germain and Barcelona.

The 26-year-old Italy forward injured his right leg against Belgium in the Nations League this week but the latest issue was with his left leg, Fabregas said.

stories.headline: F1 drivers face unique Las Vegas dilemma as GTA VI arrives: Who's playing?
stories.summary: Formula 1's drivers have a unique conundrum this week -- how to dovetail their racing duties at the Las Vegas Grand Prix alongside playing the newly released Grand Theft Auto VI.
stories.body:
Formula 1's drivers have a unique conundrum this week -- how to dovetail their racing duties at the Las Vegas Grand Prix alongside playing the newly-released Grand Theft Auto VI.

Rockstar's sixth instalment of the GTA franchise was release on Nov. 19, right in line with the beginning of the Vegas race schedule.

With 13 years between GTA V and GTA VI, it's been one of the most highly anticipated and hyped games in modern times. Speaking on Thursday night, with half the world already playing it due to the Vegas time zone, Kimi Antonelli admitted he had been bugging friends in Italy for updates.

"I've already downloaded it. I pre-ordered, I did everything. I will ask my dad to bring over the PlayStation," the newly-crowned 2026 world champion told Canadian broadcaster TSN.

"In my free time I will play. Many of us have been waiting for this game and we're all super excited.

"My friends right now are playing it. There's a friend of mine who should be going to work tomorrow. But actually is not going to sleep so he's going to work after playing all night. I've been video calling him all night on WhatsApp, 'how is the game, how is it going?' and everything, he's been showing me.

"It feels like going back 10 years. Feel like a little kid again being so excited for a game. Definitely, I'll be playing, after the weekend in my free time."

Seven-time world champion Lewis Hamilton has made no secret in recent weeks of his anticipation to play it.

The Ferrari driver suggested he will instead be focusing on preparing properly for the weekend.

"I have my console with me [but] I have the F1 game with me," he said. "That's the one I use on a race weekend because that's the thing that will ultimately help me get the result I ultimately need. I can't wait. I think everyone's been waiting to play it."

Speaking at a fan event later, however, Hamilton admitted GTA is very much on the agenda for this weekend.

"Thursday night I'll be back at the hotel early," he said to loud cheers from the audience. I hope you can tap into the kid you are [when the game is out]."

- Antonelli handed grid penalty for Las Vegas GP; Russell sets pace in FP2

- F1 bosses confirm 'agreement' on V8 engine return deal

- FIA to introduce full-time stewards to address worries over decision-making

The rest of the grid appeared to be working out when they might be able to squeeze in some time on the game around their marketing and racing appearances.

Red Bull's Max Verstappen is famous for racing late into the night on sim racing -- something Red Bull once had to ask him to stop doing, especially when he would do it over race weekends.

"It's already pre-downloaded," the four-time world champion said. "Whenever I have the time I will play. I used to play the previous one also. Of course, my life has changed a little bit compared to then. In a way it's clear the mind sometimes, it's nice and relaxing to do these things."

Verstappen's teammate Isack Hadjar even managed to squeeze in 25 minutes on Thursday, thanks to having with him a PlayStation 5 on a European server.

"I got to play really briefly before having to leave to the track so I'm still on the opening scenes," he said.

Asked by TSN when he will play it during the Vegas race, he laughed and said: "The whole time! Honestly. Hopefully it won't have an impact on my weekend."

Mercedes driver George Russell said: "I did play San Andreas when I was younger. I have been seeing some of the videos and it has given me a bit of the bug. I don't have a console with me. I definitely will give it a whirl."

Drivers should be able to find plenty of downtime to play, especially given the timing of the Vegas race.

The earliest track action begins on Thursday and Friday is 4.30 p.m. local time, and the race itself on Saturday is not until 8 p.m.

F1's Vegas race is followed by a trip to the Middle East, with an event in Qatar on Nov. 29. and Abu Dhabi on Dec. 6 to close out the season.

Alpine's Pierre Gasly, who often plays Call of Duty online against Hamilton, admitted he was kicking himself not to have prepared properly to play in Vegas, although he was already thinking about when he can get his hands on the game.

He said: "I usually bring my laptop. I've left it home -- big mistake! I'll definitely download the game after I get back after the weekend and get on it before Qatar. I love a gaming session, for me it's a nice way to relax."

Williams driver Alex Albon was also regretting his planning, saying: "I was looking into portable [consoles]. If anyone wants to give me one, I'll take it! I think I'll be in my hotel room a fair bit the next few weeks."

McLaren's Lando Norris said that he was banned from playing it growing up and that he would have to reply on his friend's PlayStation.

"I would love to, but I wasn't allowed to play it when I was younger," he said. "I wasn't allowed. So when we would go on a school trip and I could nick someone else's PSP or something, it was the best trip of my life because I could finally get to play it.

"But I never grew up playing it when I was at home. I never really played it when I was older, therefore. So it's never been my thing. But I know a lot of people around the world are playing it right now. So maybe my mind changes. But for now, it's a no."

His teammate Oscar Piastri admitted the craze might have passed him by when he was younger.

"I was far too young for the previous GTA so I've not played before. I don't know," he said. "I don't have any plans [to play] at this point in time. I know there's been a lot of hype around it. If a few people pull my arm then I might have to jump on as well!"

Alpine's Franco Colapinto had no clue the game was out this week.

"Oh, it's out?" he asked when told about it.

"What does it come in? PlayStation? I don't play video games. I thought it had already come out. I saw too many videos, people playing it no?"

When told some people had got their hands on pre-release versions, he laughed and said: "Oh, they were cheating!?" He added: "I don't play video games so much. I was in the simulator since I was very young, so that was like my video game. Not really others.

"I'm quite useless with FIFA [now called EA FC]. When I play with friends I'm not very good at it."

stories.headline: 'No one saw it coming': Inside the Swans' draft heist that landed a Lions Academy star
stories.summary: The Swans are notorious for bidding on draft night. But no one saw their heist of Lions Academy star Caylen Murray coming, given they didn't even meet his family. Jasper Chellappah looks into the fascinating happenings on night one of the AFL Draft.
stories.body:
Caylen Murray is the earliest pick to have his club-tied matching rights passed up in AFL Draft history. No one saw it coming, not even the Lions.

Make no mistake, this was a Sydney draft heist months in the making. The Swans ran the numbers and it showed Brisbane was three misly points short of matching a bid at pick 9. They pulled the trigger and watched on for five agonising minutes as trade partners disappeared one by one.

The three-time premiers were scrambling and the scenes unfolding inside their corporate box were increasingly uncomfortable. Each phone call was shorter than the last as candidates dried up in a race against time to find three points.

Up until that stage Sydney had not shown serious interest in Murray. They surely wouldn't bid on him without any leaks of interest from their camp; they surely couldn't bid on him without meeting his family.

A smokescreen devised in pre-draft analysis and 12 months of assessing Murray's talents was pulled at the perfect time to rip him out of Queensland. They feigned disinterest and caught the Lions napping. No one saw it coming, not least Brisbane's war room.

'Bidney' has been up to these tricks before. They'd made 11 bids in 10 years prior to last night, including Brisbane's own prospect Sam Marshall. They nearly snared Adelaide's Max Michalanney with a similar ploy in 2022.

As the dust settles, it's clear to see the Lions were undone by new draft rules that they themselves necessitated.

In 2022 they used 34, 35, 38, 40, and 41 to match Will Ashcroft's bid at pick 2. In 2024 they used 40, 42, 43, and 46 to match Levi Ashcroft's bid at pick 5. In 2025 they used 22, 23, and 39 to match a bid at pick 6 for Dan Annable. They achieved similar results for first-round talents Jaspa Fletcher and Marshall.

Brisbane had played the system to perfection up until Thursday night. But new draft rules require clubs to find the points to match with a maximum of two draft picks. A new draft value index (DVI) inflated the worth of top 10 picks. And a new levy added a 20% tax to bids matched by grand finalists.

Brisbane was caught looking too far ahead by sliding pick 19 down to 24 and 34. The 1355-point value of pick 9 became 1626 points with the grand finalist loading. Brisbane's picks 24 and 25 were worth 1211 points and they could go into a maximum of 412 points deficit on their future first-rounder. Tallied up and they accounted for 1623 of the 1626 points required.

The AFL values that gap at 1/1000th of the worth of the 3000 points Dougie Cochrane was matched with.

Sydney pulled off a coup to rival footy's very best off-field drama in 2026.

Brisbane's shortcoming wasn't just to the Swans's benefit, either. Gustavo Teixeira landed in St Kilda's lap at pick 11, a genuine pick one chance throughout the season. The flow-on effect kept coming with Collingwood grabbing their top target in mad Pies fan Sam Gayfer. Without the bid being matched these clubs effectively moved up the draft order.

Murray's shock was plain to see as reality set in. But the star academy graduate quickly recovered to deliver an extremely mature interview.

"I didn't realise Sydney was that keen but [I'm] stoked to join the club. It's an amazing club, great players, great staff and I'm keen to explore Sydney.

"It was a bit of a shock at the start but now it's sunk in. I'm stoked to be a Swans player."

The classy and composed halfback looms as a natural replacement for departed All-Australian Nick Blakey.

stories.headline: Kayla Harrison, Amanda Nunes reclaim leading roles in women's P4P top 10
stories.summary: Who do Kayla Harrison and Amanda Nunes replace in ESPN's P4P women's top 10?
stories.body:
Hello (again), Kayla Harrison and Amanda Nunes. Goodbye (for now), Valentina Shevchenko and Zhang Weili. The top of the ESPN women's MMA pound-for-pound rankings has a new look.

Harrison and Nunes, both of whom had been ineligible for the top 10 because of inactivity, returned over the weekend for a clash of elites at UFC 334. Harrison, defending her bantamweight championship for the first time after nearly a year and a half out of the cage while healing from surgery for herniated discs in her neck, scored a fourth-round submission of Nunes, who had been retired for nearly 3½ years. As a result, Harrison takes over the No. 1 ranking and Nunes, a former two-division champion and the consensus GOAT of women's MMA, is No. 2.

The former occupants of those spots, Shevchenko and Zhang, are newly ineligible for the rankings because it's been over a year since they have fought and they have nothing scheduled. Those two former champions drop out, and the rest of the women's top 10 remains the same.

In the men's rankings, UFC heavyweight champion Ciryl Gane moves up one spot to No. 7 on the strength of his decision win over Josh Hokit in their title bout at UFC 334.

For the ESPN divisional MMA rankings, click here.

Note: Results are current; rankings are as of Nov. 18. To be eligible for the rankings, a fighter must have competed over the past 12 months or must have an upcoming fight booked. Fighters who have been dropped for inactivity can be reinstated only after they compete.

Women's pound-for-pound rankings

1. Kayla Harrison

UFC bantamweight champion

Previous ranking: Unranked

Record: 20-1

Last: W (Sub4) vs. Amanda Nunes, Nov. 14

Next: TBA

Harrison stepped into the Octagon at UFC 334 already a reigning champion, but her submission win over Nunes was truly her crowning achievement. The backstory about their shared training gym history added drama to the buildup, but what mattered most about this matchup was that Harrison, who had voiced her goal to be the greatest ever in women's MMA, was facing the woman who has lived up to that standard. After choking out Nunes, what can Harrison do for an encore? Can any other woman in the sport give her a fight? Maybe it won't come to that. Harrison and Nunes both called for a rematch -- but at featherweight. That would lessen Harrison's burden in dealing with her toughest foe: the weigh-in scale.

2. Amanda Nunes

UFC bantamweight

Previous ranking: Unranked

Record: 23-6

Last: L (Sub4) vs. Kayla Harrison, Nov. 14

Next: TBA

Nunes' return from retirement did not go as she had hoped, but her failing was not so much about deteriorated physical abilities as it was about her ill-advised choice to venture too much into the grappling wheelhouse of Harrison, a two-time Olympic judo gold medalist. If Nunes gets the rematch both women are calling for, but this time at 145 pounds, that would seem to be to the advantage of Harrison, the bigger woman. But a redo would give Nunes another opportunity to lean into her own prodigious strength as a striker.

3. Cris Cyborg

PFL featherweight champion

Record: 30-2, 1 NC

Last: W (UD) vs. Ketlen Vieira, Aug. 22

Next: TBA

It had been a while since Cyborg had fought an elite opponent in MMA until she met Larissa Pacheco in 2024. That was a legitimate matchup -- and many within the industry were predicting Cyborg's downfall. Instead, she took out the PFL's two-weight champion, upending all of Pacheco's momentum. One of the original pioneers of women's MMA is once again a champion after getting her second career submission at PFL Lyon in December. The PFL promoted her fight with Vieira as a retirement bout, but after her win Cyborg did not sound like someone who is done fighting.

4. Natalia Silva

UFC flyweight champion

Record: 21-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Wang Cong, Oct. 3

Next: TBA

Silva was looking every bit the part of a future UFC champion following a dominant display against Alexa Grasso at UFC 315 and a victory over Rose Namajunas at UFC 324. And now she has fulfilled that expectation, beating Wang at UFC 332 to win the belt vacated by injured Valentina Shevchenko. Silva's stick-and-move style has frustrated even the highest level of opponent, and she's got youth on her side as she won't turn 30 until 2027.

5. Mackenzie Dern

UFC strawweight champion

Record: 17-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Gillian Robertson, Aug. 15

Next: TBA

Dern's rise to the 115-pound throne was truly a changing of the guard. She is the division's first first-time champion since 2019, because the previous three champs -- Zhang Weili, Carla Esparza and Rose Namajunas -- all were in their second reigns. Dern, nearly a decade into her MMA career after multiple jiu-jitsu world championships, has won four fights in a row, including a dominant performance against a fellow grappling-heavy fighter, Robertson, in her first title defense.

6. Alexa Grasso

UFC flyweight

Record: 18-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Manon Fiorot, Sept. 12

Next: TBA

Grasso went nearly three years without winning a fight, but her 2023 win right before the skid was a huge one, a submission of Valentina Shevchenko for the UFC title. What followed were two more fights with Shevchenko -- a draw, then a loss -- and then a loss to Natalia Silva. But she reasserted herself with a finish of Maycee Barber in March, then got the best of Fiorot, a fellow title contender, at Noche UFC to put herself in position for another title shot.

7. Tatiana Suarez

UFC strawweight

Record: 13-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Virna Jandiroba, Nov. 7

Next: TBA

If Suarez was still feeling the effects of last year's humbling defeat to Zhang Weili in a title challenge, she certainly didn't show it at UFC 327, overcoming early adversity to thrash Loopy Godínez. Then she went on to beat another fellow top-10 strawweight, Jandiroba, sending a message to the division that Suarez is going to be a tough out for anyone at 115 pounds.

8. Dakota Ditcheva

PFL flyweight

Record: 16-0

Last: W (UD) vs. Denise Kielholtz, July 31

Next: TBA

Not only did Ditcheva win the PFL's flyweight season in 2024, but she did so in spectacular fashion -- a TKO finish over Taila Santos, who once challenged for a UFC title. Ditcheva fought only once in 2025, dominating Sumiko Inaba in the co-main event of the first PFL Champions Series card in Cape Town, South Africa. She then spent over a year on the sideline, healing injuries to both hands, before returning at PFL New York with a dominant win over Kielholtz.

9. Manon Fiorot

UFC flyweight

Record: 13-3

Last: L (UD) vs. Alexa Grasso, Sept. 12

Next: TBA

Fiorot had handled everyone the UFC put in front of her -- except the champion, Valentina Shevchenko, who defeated the Frenchwoman at UFC 315 in May 2025. But then, with another title shot within her grasp, Fiorot ran into Grasso, a former champion, at Noche UFC and lost a competitive fight.

10. Jasmine Jasudavicius

UFC flyweight

Record: 16-4

Last: W (UD) vs. Erin Blanchfield, Oct. 17

Next: TBA

Jasudavicius was rising in the 125-pound division until being knocked out by Manon Fiorot last year, halting a five-fight winning streak. But she got back up and won two in a row, most recently an impressive grappling performance against Blanchfield, to reassert herself as a contender.

Other fighter receiving votes: Joselyne Edwards and Virna Jandiroba.

How our panel voted
Brett Okamoto: 1. Kayla Harrison; 2. Amanda Nunes; 3. Mackenzie Dern; 4. Natalia Silva; 5. Tatiana Suarez; 6. Cris Cyborg; 7. Alexa Grasso; 8. Manon Fiorot; 9. Dakota Ditcheva; 10. Virna Jandiroba.

Carlos Contreras Legaspi: 1. Harrison; 2. Cyborg; 3. Silva; 4. Nunes; 5. Dern; 6. Grasso; 7. Ditcheva; 8. Suarez; 9. Fiorot; 10. Jasmine Jasudavicius.

Andrew Davis: 1. Harrison; 2. Nunes; 3. Cyborg; 4. Silva; 5. Dern; 6. Grasso; 7. Ditcheva; 8. Fiorot; 9. Suarez; 10. Jasudavicius.

Dre Waters: 1. Harrison; 2. Cyborg; 3. Nunes; 4. Dern; 5. Silva; 6. Grasso; 7. Ditcheva; 8. Suarez; 9. Fiorot; 10. Joselyne Edwards.

Jeff Wagenheim: 1. Harrison; 2. Nunes; 3. Cyborg; 4. Silva; 5. Grasso; 6. Dern; 7. Fiorot; 8. Suarez; 9. Ditcheva; 10. Jasudavicius.

Men's pound-for-pound rankings

1. Islam Makhachev

UFC welterweight champion

Record: 29-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Ian Machado Garry, Aug. 15

Next: TBA

Makhachev vacated the UFC lightweight championship to go for a second title at welterweight. By winning that belt last November with a thrashing of Jack Della Maddalena, Makhachev staked his place among MMA's greatest -- not just in today's sport but of all time. His win over Machado Garry at UFC 330 was his 17th straight, breaking the UFC record for consecutive wins. Makhachev is piling up unprecedented achievements.

2. Alexander Volkanovski

UFC featherweight champion

Record: 29-4

Last: W (TKO2) vs. Movsar Evloev, Oct. 24

Next: TBA

It felt as if the sport had started to write Volkanovski's eulogy following his knockout loss to Ilia Topuria in February 2024. Volkanovski noticed and made a point of proving to everyone he still has plenty left by recapturing the featherweight belt at UFC 314, the first of two consecutive wins over Lopes. His age (38) will likely continue to be a prefight topic, which is fine because Volkanovski enjoys proving people wrong. He did just that by handing Evloev his first loss at UFC 333.

3. Petr Yan

UFC bantamweight champion

Record: 21-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Merab Dvalishvili, Oct. 24

Next: TBA

What a return to the top it's been for Yan. He began his career with 15 consecutive wins before going on a 1-4 run from 2021 to 2023. That almost doesn't feel real now, after watching him reclaim his throne against Dvalishvili, who once handed him the worst loss of his career, then completing his trilogy with Dvalishvili with a successful title defense. Yan took a major detour, but this was the destination we felt he was capable of before the skid. He once again looks like one of the best fighters on the planet.

4. Ilia Topuria

UFC lightweight

Record: 17-1

Last: L (TKO4) vs. Justin Gaethje, June 14

Next: TBA

Topuria was an undefeated two-division champion when he ran into Gaethje at UFC Freedom 250 and was brutalized in a stoppage loss. How will that affect the immediate future of Topuria? His knockout wins over two of the greatest featherweights, Alexander Volkanovski and Max Holloway, gave him an intimidating aura. Can the former champion get that back?

5. Justin Gaethje

UFC lightweight champion

Record: 28-5

Last: W (TKO4) vs. Ilia Topuria, June 14

Next: TBA

Gaethje has spent his 15-year career thrilling MMA fans, but before the title bout on the White House lawn, all he had to show for it -- aside from 15 bonus checks in 15 UFC appearances -- were two missed opportunities to be an undisputed champion. His fourth-round TKO of Topuria got Gaethje over the hump. It was a resilient performance in a back-and-forth battle that is a prime candidate for fight of the year. More important for Gaethje: At age 37, he is finally sitting at the top of the mountain.

6. Joshua Van

UFC flyweight champion

Record: 18-2

Last: W (UD) vs. Alexandre Pantoja, Sept. 19

Next: Jan. 30 vs. Manel Kape

Van has been champion since December, but until UFC 331, there were doubters. Van had been handed the belt by default, when his challenge for the title was waved off after 26 seconds because Pantoja dislocated his left elbow. Van went on to defend the title against Tatsuro Taira in May, then faced Pantoja in a rematch at UFC 331. Van produced a clear victory -- his eighth win in a row -- to leave no doubt who rules at 125 pounds.

7. Ciryl Gane

UFC heavyweight champion

Previous ranking: Tied for 8th

Record: 15-2, 1 NC

Last: W (UD) vs. Josh Hokit, Nov. 14

Next: TBA

Gane is unique in that he is the first -- and could very well go down as the only -- heavyweight to face the division's four biggest names in Francis Ngannou, Jon Jones, Tom Aspinall and Pereira. None of those four have fought each other, yet all four have have fought the Frenchman. Gane was 0-2 with a no-contest against that group before he knocked out Pereira in the second round of their interim title fight on the White House lawn. Gane was elevated to undisputed champ after Aspinall, still injured, vacated his title, and the new champ made his first defense against Hokit at UFC 334, winning a slugfest.

8. Arman Tsarukyan

UFC lightweight

Previous ranking: 7

Record: 24-3

Last: W (KO1) vs. Mauricio Ruffy, Sept. 19

Next: TBA

Tsarukyan is right back in the place he was in January 2025 -- on the cusp of a title fight. He withdrew from a challenge of Islam Makhachev one day before UFC 311 because of a back injury, and later in the year he was passed over twice when the UFC was booking lightweight title bouts. But by knocking out Ruffy with an elbow in the first round at UFC 331, Tsarukyan put himself back at the front of the line.

9. Merab Dvalishvili

UFC bantamweight

Previous ranking: Tied for 8th

Record: 21-6

Last: L (UD) vs. Petr Yan, Oct. 24

Next: TBA

Dvalishvili was on one of the most impressive runs through the UFC's bantamweight division ever. Not only did he defeat Sean O'Malley for the second time in nine months at UFC 316, but he showcased a new part of his game, finishing O'Malley with a guillotine. Starting in August 2022, Dvalishvili beat José Aldo, Yan, Henry Cejudo, O'Malley (twice), Umar Nurmagomedov and Cory Sandhagen. But at UFC 323, in an attempt to become the first champion in UFC history to successfully defend a title four times in a calendar year, Dvalishvili lost a rematch with Yan. Their third meeting at UFC 333 was the most competitive in their trilogy, but Dvalishvili fell short again.

10. Alex Pereira

UFC heavyweight

Record: 13-4

Last: L (TKO2) vs. Ciryl Gane, June 14

Next: Dec. 12 vs. Sergei Pavlovich

Pereira made a big splash in the MMA after a world championship career in kickboxing. He joined the UFC in 2021 and became a middleweight champion the following year, then moved on to be a two-time light heavyweight titlist before making an unprecedented bid for a belt in a third weight class when he fought Game at UFC Freedom 250 for an interim heavyweight title. Pereira got knocked out in that fight, but now he's back on his feet and in position to reclaim his position when he faces a fellow title contender, Pavlovich, at UFC 335.

Other fighters receiving votes: Alexandre Pantoja and Sean Strickland.

How our panel voted
Brett Okamoto: 1. Islam Makhachev; 2. Petr Yan; 3. Ilia Topuria; 4. Alexander Volkanovski; 5. Joshua Van; 6. Arman Tsarukyan; 7. Merab Dvalishvili; 8. Ciryl Gane; 9. Alex Pereira; 10. Justin Gaethje.
